## What the site is

copyonline.co.uk is the UK's practical authority for anyone who has to write commercial copy
themselves — the founder drafting a homepage, the in-house marketer composing a product email,
the junior copywriter learning the craft. It teaches copywriting as a learnable discipline
through thorough guides, worked examples, checklists and reference material covering web
pages, ads, email, product descriptions and tone of voice, and it lets visitors test their own
drafts immediately with free browser-based tools: a headline scorer, a readability and clarity
checker, a call-to-action tester, and a length and character counter. The site earns its
authority by showing its working — explaining the principle behind every rule, not just
issuing instructions — and by staying squarely on the question of copy quality, leaving
channel strategy to advertise.co.uk, search visibility to websitepromotion.co.uk and SEO
tooling to seotools.co.uk.

## Who it is for

**Primary:** UK founders, in-house marketers and small-business owners who must write their own commercial copy and know it matters but have no formal training — they are sitting in front of a blank page for a product page, ad or welcome email and need practical craft guidance right now

**Secondary:** Freelance and junior copywriters building their skills and professional vocabulary; agency teams who need a reliable reference to send clients or brief against; non-native English writers working in UK commercial contexts who need ASA/CAP-aware guidance


## What the reader came to do

- Understand how to write a specific type of copy (homepage, product page, email subject line, ad headline, CTA, tone-of-voice document) with a concrete method they can follow
- Check or improve a draft they have already written using a free browser tool
- Learn the principles behind good commercial copy — why certain structures work, what motivates a reader to act
- Find a checklist they can run through before publishing or sending
- See a worked example or before-and-after rewrite of copy similar to their own
- Understand UK-specific constraints: ASA/CAP rules for ads, plain English expectations, sector-specific tone considerations
- Get a quick reference answer to a specific copywriting question (word counts, subject-line length, CTA button copy conventions)
- Understand tone of voice — how to define, document and apply a consistent brand voice across channels

## How it differs from the neighbours

The obvious UK competitors are: Copyblogger (US-centric, content marketing focus, not
commercial copy craft), the Drum (trade news, not a teaching resource), ProCopywriters (member
association, not a teaching or tool site), Hemingway App (single readability dimension, no
copy-type guidance, no UK context), CoSchedule Headline Studio (headline tool only, US-framed,
paywalled for full use). copyonline.co.uk is distinct in three ways: (1) it is explicitly UK-
registered in voice, spelling, and regulatory context (ASA/CAP throughout); (2) it combines
editorial craft teaching with free browser tools in one place, so a reader can read the guide
and immediately test their draft without leaving; (3) its editorial layout — warm paper
background, serif display headings, reading-first — is deliberately unlike both the tool-
portal aesthetic of seotools.co.uk and the magazine-grid of designblog.co.uk, signalling a
different kind of authority. The Sarah Turner Agency YouTube content surfaced in research
targets freelance copywriters building businesses (invoicing, client acquisition, community);
copyonline.co.uk targets people writing copy, not people running copywriting businesses — a
distinct and underserved intent.

## Voice and stance

Copy is a craft with learnable rules, not a talent or a mystery — this site is for people who
want to understand exactly why something works, shown through real examples, and it is against
vague inspiration, generic 'content tips' and the pretence that AI output needs no human
judgement or editing.

## Must nots

- Must not build, stub, reference, or imply a copywriter directory, marketplace, or brief board at launch — the commercial slot is prepared but gated; no 'coming soon' messaging, no category page, no placeholder
- Must not duplicate SEO tools, keyword research tools, or search-ranking guidance — that territory belongs to seotools.co.uk; copy quality and SEO copy are mentioned only to the extent of writing clarity for human readers
- Must not duplicate advertising channel guidance, media planning, or ad spend advice — that belongs to advertise.co.uk; ad copywriting craft is in scope, channel selection is not
- Must not duplicate site-promotion or traffic-acquisition content — that belongs to websitepromotion.co.uk
- Must not use negative-identity framing ('we are not an agency', 'unlike freelancers') in any public-facing copy
- Must not present as a regulated communications or legal-advice service — CAP/ASA references are practical craft notes, not compliance consultancy, and must be clearly labelled as such
- Must not publish a news feed, blog roll, or listing page that would be empty at launch or require a live external data source the portfolio does not yet have
- Must not use the shared estate CTA red (#8b0000) — colour palette must be clearly distinct from designblog.co.uk (#C0392B accent) and advertise.co.uk (#E8490F accent); the brief proposes deep teal primary with warm amber accent on warm paper
- Must not hype or advocate for AI writing tools as a replacement for human copywriting judgement — the stance is that copy is a craft requiring human skill and editorial decision-making
- Must not reproduce copyrighted copy examples without transformation or attribution

## The directory / marketplace slot (prepared, NOT built)

A directory of UK copywriters — with entries carrying specialisation, sector experience, day
rate range, and portfolio link — is the natural commercial slot for this domain, consistent
with the old marketplace heritage. It is explicitly gated behind the bugs_open/444 condition
and must not be built or implied until that gate is cleared. When it is built, it replaces no
existing content but adds a new top-level section. No directory content should be planned,
stubbed, or referenced in live copy at launch.

## Tools it proposes

- **Headline Scorer** — Headline quality is the highest-leverage single intervention in commercial copy and there is no free, UK-focused, browser-based tool that scores headlines with plain-English feedback rather than a US-centric emotional-marketing framing — A headline or subject line of up to 100 characters — Numeric score (0–100) with breakdowns for word count, power-word presence, emotional vs rational balance, clarity, and character count against platform limits; three specific improvement suggestions
- **Readability and Clarity Checker** — Commercial copy clarity is distinct from academic readability; existing tools (Hemingway, Grammarly) are US-English-biased or paywalled; this is a direct, fast, no-login alternative for UK practitioners — A block of commercial copy, minimum 50 words — Flesch-Kincaid reading age, average sentence length, passive-voice sentence count and percentage, jargon-flag list (industry terms detected), overall clarity verdict (Clear / Review / Revise) with highlighted problem sentences
- **Call-to-Action Tester** — CTA copy is under-served by existing tools which check grammar but not persuasive structure; a focused CTA tester fills a clear gap for the non-specialist writer who knows their CTA is weak but not why — A CTA phrase (1–8 words) and optional context field (what the page or email is about) — Rating on verb strength (weak/moderate/strong), specificity score, estimated character count vs platform norms, pattern match against high-performing CTA structures, and three alternative CTA suggestions
- **Length and Character Counter** — Writers constantly context-switch between formats with different constraints; a single reference tool that shows all format limits simultaneously against a live count saves the tab-switching and mental arithmetic that slows down real work — Pasted copy of any length — Live word count, character count with spaces, character count without spaces, and a comparison table showing whether the paste fits within recommended limits for: Google Ads headline, Google Ads description, email subject line, SMS (160 chars), LinkedIn post, Twitter/X post, meta title, meta description, Amazon product title
- **Tone-of-Voice Consistency Checker** — Brand voice consistency is a known pain point for growing teams and agencies managing multiple writers; no free browser tool currently addresses this; it directly supports the tone-of-voice guide content — Two or more text samples labelled as being from the same brand — Side-by-side analysis of formality register (formal/neutral/casual score per sample), pronoun balance (we/you ratio), average sentence length per sample, vocabulary overlap score, and a consistency verdict with flagged divergences

## The 24 planned pages

### Core (10)

- **How to Write a Homepage** *(guide)* — A step-by-step guide covering the above-the-fold value proposition, the hierarchy of sections, headline and subheading patterns, CTA placement, and social proof — with annotated worked examples of real homepage structures. The most-searched copywriting task for non-specialists.
- **How to Write a Product Page** *(guide)* — Covers feature-to-benefit translation, scannable structure, sensory and specificity language, handling objections, and the difference between product copy for e-commerce listings versus dedicated landing pages. Includes a before-and-after rewrite.
- **How to Write Email Copy That Gets Opened and Read** *(guide)* — Covers subject lines, preview text, opening hooks, body structure, single-CTA discipline, and sign-off tone — separately for cold outreach, welcome sequences, and promotional emails. UK spam and PECR context noted.
- **How to Write Ad Copy: Search, Social and Display** *(guide)* — Character-constrained copywriting for Google Ads headlines and descriptions, Meta ad primary text, and display banners — covering the hook-benefit-CTA structure, emotional triggers, and ASA/CAP compliance notes for UK advertisers. Links out to advertise.co.uk for channel strategy and spend.
- **Tone of Voice: How to Define and Document Yours** *(guide)* — A practical guide to identifying brand voice attributes, writing a tone-of-voice document, applying it consistently across touchpoints, and testing whether it is actually being followed. Includes a downloadable-style framework and worked example for a hypothetical UK brand.
- **How to Write a Call to Action** *(guide)* — Covers the difference between button copy, link copy and inline CTAs; the psychology of action verbs and specificity; where on a page CTAs perform best; and common mistakes. Paired with the CTA Tester tool.
- **Headline Scorer** *(tool)* — A browser tool that takes a headline and scores it across dimensions including word count, power-word density, emotional vs rational balance, clarity, and specificity — returning a score and plain-English improvement suggestions. No login required.
- **Readability and Clarity Checker** *(tool)* — Paste in a block of copy and receive a Flesch-Kincaid readability level, average sentence length, passive-voice count, jargon flags, and a summary clarity verdict with specific sentence-level suggestions. Aimed at commercial copy, not academic prose.
- **Call-to-Action Tester** *(tool)* — Input a CTA phrase (button or link copy) and receive a verdict on verb strength, specificity, length, and whether it matches common high-performing CTA patterns — with alternative suggestions generated from the input context.
- **Length and Character Counter** *(tool)* — A real-time counter that shows word count, character count with and without spaces, and compares the result against recommended lengths for common copy types: Google Ads headlines, email subject lines, meta descriptions, Twitter/X posts, SMS, and LinkedIn updates. Paste-and-go, no account needed.

### Valuable (10)

- **The Copywriter's Glossary** *(guide)* — Plain-English definitions of the terms practitioners use — above the fold, AIDA, benefit vs feature, body copy, conversion copy, direct response, lift, USP, and 60+ more — with a one-line example for each. A reference page that earns repeat visits and links.
- **UK Advertising Rules for Copywriters: ASA and CAP Plain-English Guide** *(guide)* — A practical summary of what the ASA CAP Code requires of commercial copy — claims that need substantiation, comparative advertising rules, rules for specific sectors (finance, health, alcohol, children), and what 'misleading' means in practice. Not legal advice; a craft reference with links to CAP guidance.
- **How to Write a Landing Page** *(guide)* — Distinct from the homepage guide: covers single-offer pages, the no-navigation principle, long-form vs short-form decisions, trust signals, and objection handling in a conversion context. Includes annotated structural diagram and worked example.
- **Copywriting Formulas: AIDA, PAS, BAB and Beyond** *(guide)* — An honest assessment of the classic formulas — what each is, when it works, when it fails, and how to adapt them. Shows each formula applied to the same brief so readers can compare outputs directly.
- **How to Write for Different Audiences: B2B vs B2C** *(guide)* — Covers the structural and tonal differences between business-to-business and consumer copy, with examples — decision-maker vs end-user framing, technical depth, proof requirements, and urgency tactics.
- **The Copy Clinic: Before-and-After Rewrites** *(editorial)* — A recurring editorial series taking real (anonymised or reconstructed) examples of weak commercial copy — homepage headlines, product descriptions, email subject lines — and rewriting them with a running commentary explaining every change. Shows the craft rather than just stating rules.
- **Copy Length Reference Tables** *(data)* — A single-page reference giving the recommended and maximum character and word counts for every major copy format: Google Ads, Meta Ads, email subject lines, SMS, LinkedIn, meta titles and descriptions, Amazon product titles, app store descriptions, and more — with source and last-verified date.
- **Checklists: Copy Review Before You Publish** *(guide)* — Format-specific checklists — one each for homepages, product pages, email campaigns, ads, and landing pages — that a writer can run through before sign-off. Each item is a yes/no question with a one-line explanation of why it matters.
- **How to Brief a Copywriter** *(guide)* — For the audience member who occasionally hires rather than writes: what a good copy brief contains, how to explain target audience and tone, how to give useful feedback, and what makes a brief fail. Bridges the gap between the writing audience and the prepared-but-not-yet-live marketplace slot.
- **Writing for the Web: Scanning, Structure and Microcopy** *(guide)* — Covers how people read on screens (they do not), the F-pattern, chunking, subheading hierarchy, bullet discipline, link text, button labels, form microcopy and error messages. A craft guide for the full digital copywriting context.

### Aspirational (4)

- **What Makes a Headline Work: Analysis of High-Performing UK Copy** *(research)* — An original analysis of structural and linguistic patterns in high-performing headlines across UK e-commerce, SaaS, and direct-response contexts — identifying patterns in word count, emotional triggers, specificity and structure. Citeable and linkable; builds authority.
- **Tone-of-Voice Consistency Checker** *(tool)* — Paste two or more blocks of copy from the same brand; the tool flags tonal inconsistencies in formality level, pronoun choice, sentence length variance, and vocabulary register. Useful for brands reviewing copy across channels.
- **Copywriting for E-commerce: Category Pages, Product Listings, and Basket Copy** *(guide)* — A deep guide to the specific copy challenges of online retail — writing at scale for product listings, the role of category page copy, basket and checkout reassurance copy, and post-purchase email tone. UK retail context throughout.
- **The House View: Copywriting Positions We Hold** *(editorial)* — A short standing editorial page stating the site's explicit positions on contested copywriting questions — long copy vs short copy, AI-assisted writing, the Oxford comma in UK copy, active vs passive voice as a rule — with the reasoning shown. Creates a defined editorial identity.

## Open questions the brief itself raises

- Colour palette: the brief suggests deep teal primary with warm amber accent on warm paper — specific hex values need owner sign-off before design begins to ensure clear differentiation from all estate siblings
- Tool build approach: the four specified browser tools (headline scorer, readability checker, CTA tester, length counter) need a technical decision on whether they are client-side JavaScript (no backend, instant, private) or server-side (allows logging, improvement over time) — this affects both the build plan and the privacy copy
- The 'canary duties' listed in the portfolio entry (chrome pin experiment runbook §5, planner imagery prompt §5b, discovery-before-plan §2b) are referenced but not explained in the brief materials — a human should confirm what these require of this site specifically before the planner runs
- Tone-of-voice consistency checker is listed as aspirational because it is technically more complex than the other four tools — owner should confirm whether this is in scope for the initial build or a named later addition
- The 'How to Brief a Copywriter' guide intentionally gestures toward the future marketplace slot without claiming it — owner should confirm this framing is acceptable or whether even indirect reference should be avoided until the 444 gate is cleared
- UK legal review: the ASA/CAP guide section should be reviewed by someone with CAP Code familiarity before publication to confirm the 'practical craft notes, not compliance advice' framing is sufficient and no disclaimer wording is needed
- writesy.uk is named in the portfolio entry as a 'twin by craft' sibling — no brief exists for it in the materials provided, so the exact boundary between copyonline.co.uk (commercial copy) and writesy.uk (writer's instrument) has not been confirmed; a human should define this boundary before content commissioning begins to prevent overlap

## Research quality (the writer's own assessment)

thin — the web research returned no pages from the domain itself (it does not yet exist) and
surfaced entirely unrelated content (Illinois DCFS FOIA page, Wirecutter data-privacy article,
GWI consumer profiling guide, a CliffsNotes marketing Q&A); the one partially relevant result
was a US-focused YouTube video about freelance copywriting business tools, not UK copy craft;
all brief content is therefore drawn from the portfolio entry, the owner brief, and domain-
implied subject knowledge rather than competitive landscape research

## The one thing to eye — a known blind spot, not a new risk

**"The Copywriter's Glossary" is planned as a `guide`, not as a listing page.** That is the right
call. A glossary planned as a LISTING page is the one shape bug 444's new gate does not catch —
its own stated blind spot (register BLD-028: listing pages typed as content). As a guide, its
definitions are written inline, so it cannot ship as an empty shell. **At plan review, check it
stayed a prose guide.** If it becomes a listing page with an item source, it will ship empty
exactly as designblog's did.
